why.role_legibility: D420's lightning bolt icon paired with text on a separate line makes the warning role unmistakably distinct; F516/14AA integrate it into the header, making it blend rather than stand out.
why.visual_craft: D420's two-tier header with icon adds visual hierarchy and rhythm; D420 has better spacing cadence despite using more height. F516 and 14AA are nearly identical.
why.information_hierarchy: The lightning bolt in D420 immediately signals the critical warning (external send) at the visual center; F516/14AA require reading the text to parse the warning's importance.
why.preview_readability: All three have identical message body placement, font, and spacing; readability is indistinguishable.
why.provenance_visibility: Source line (出所) position and styling are identical across all three; equally visible without competing.
why.screen_occupation: F516 and 14AA use a single-line header requiring minimal vertical space; D420's two-line header with icon uses ~10-15% more height.
why.overall: D420's visual clarity about the external-send warning outweighs its space penalty—the icon is an affordance that prevents user error. F516 and 14AA are safer but visually quieter.

differences: D420 splits the header into two lines: '# Slack' + '⚡ 外部に出ます', introducing a lightning bolt icon
F516 and 14AA use a single-line header: '# Slack 外部に出ます' (no icon, no line break)
D420's warning text is typographically separated and icon-reinforced; F516/14AA integrate it inline
No discernible differences between F516 and 14AA—they appear to be the same design variant
